name: Space, Quantum and Cyber: Government Funded Frontier Tech
thesis: The common money source is government: the Pentagon (Golden Dome missile defense, Space Development Agency constellations), the Commerce Department and DARPA for quantum, and every enterprise and agency for cybersecurity. In space, SpaceX is the launch chokepoint and is now public (SPCX, listed June 12, 2026), worth about $2.26T at the Oct 5, 2026 close, so the rest of the group is priced against it. The investable picks around it are suppliers, satellite builders, defense primes and the few credible launch challengers. Quantum is real science and revenue is finally growing fast at IonQ, but the pure plays still trade at high multiples of small sales and keep raising money, now partly from the government in exchange for equity. Treat them as option premium sources, not compounders. Cybersecurity is the most proven cash generator of the three, and the big consolidation deals (Palo Alto with CyberArk closed; Google with Wiz cleared the EU) are done or nearly done.
money_source: Golden Dome: the administration put the cost at about $185B, but CBO estimated on May 12, 2026 that a Golden Dome style shield could cost about $1.2T over 20 years, with space based interceptors the biggest piece (about $448B without them). Congress has provided roughly $25B through the 2025 reconciliation law and about $13.4B in fiscal 2026 appropriations. Space Systems Command awarded 20 contracts worth up to $3.2B to 12 companies (including LMT, NOC, RTX and SpaceX) to prototype space based interceptors (May 2026). SDA Tranche 3 Tracking Layer awards in December 2025 totaled about $3.5B (Lockheed about $1.1B, L3Harris about $843M, Rocket Lab $816M, Northrop about $764M). SpaceX: IPO June 12, 2026; Google agreed to pay SpaceX $920M a month for AI compute at its xAI data centers from October 2026 to June 2029. EchoStar's spectrum sales to SpaceX total about $19.6B, with up to about $11.1B paid in SpaceX stock. Quantum: the Commerce Department is giving more than $2B in CHIPS Act money to nine quantum firms in exchange for minority stakes, including $100M each to D-Wave, Rigetti and Quantinuum (D-Wave's final agreement signed Sep 8, 2026). Cyber: Palo Alto closed its about $25B CyberArk deal on Feb 11, 2026, and Google's $32B Wiz deal won EU approval a day later.

facts: Rocket Lab holds more than $1.3B of Space Development Agency awards: $515M for 18 Tranche 2 Transport Layer satellites and $816M for Tranche 3 Tracking Layer missile warning satellites (December 2025).
Neutron, its medium lift reusable rocket, now targets a first launch no earlier than Q4 2026 after a stage one tank failed a pressure test in January 2026.
It closed the Geost payload deal ($275M, August 2025) and the Mynaric laser communications deal ($155.3M, April 2026) to move up from launch into defense payloads.
Because it builds satellites and parts as well as rockets, it is a picks and shovels supplier to Golden Dome style programs, not only a launcher.
Execution on Neutron is the swing factor; another slip would hit a stock priced for success.

pipeline.product: Golden Dome space based interceptor prototypes and follow on production
pipeline.timing: Prototype contracts awarded May 2026; production decisions 2027 and later
pipeline.what_changes_for_suppliers: Large new demand for interceptors, tracking satellites, ground systems and software; primes and SpaceX are already on the prototype list.

pipeline.product: SDA Tranche 2 and Tranche 3 Tracking and Transport layer satellites
pipeline.what_changes_for_suppliers: Steady production for LMT, NOC, LHX and RKLB.
A credible medium lift alternative to Falcon 9; a further delay would hit RKLB hard.

pipeline.timing: BlueBirds 11 to 13 launched Aug 5, 2026; 14 to 16 shipping to Cape Canaveral as of Sep 30, 2026
pipeline.what_changes_for_suppliers: Launch providers and phased array suppliers; each delay adds funding needs and dilution.

pipeline.product: SpaceX as a public company: first quarterly reports, Starlink Mobile growth, Google compute contract ramp
pipeline.timing: Compute contract runs Oct 2026 to Jun 2029
pipeline.what_changes_for_suppliers: Sets the valuation yardstick for every space stock; direct to cell competes with AST, Iridium and Globalstar.

pipeline.product: IBM Kookaburra module (2026) toward Starling fault tolerant system (2029, about 200 logical qubits)
pipeline.what_changes_for_suppliers: Big tech progress sets the bar that pure plays are valued against.
Creates cyber spending now, regardless of when useful quantum computers arrive.

layers.name: Launch
layers.why: Every satellite has to get to orbit; launch cadence sets the pace of the whole space economy.
layers.bottleneck_reason: SpaceX flies the large majority of US launches; credible alternatives (Rocket Lab Neutron, Blue Origin New Glenn, ULA Vulcan) are still ramping.

companies.name: SpaceX
companies.role: Falcon 9, Starship, Starlink, Starshield, AI compute (xAI data centers)
companies.note: Listed June 12, 2026. Closed at $171.09 on Oct 5, 2026 (up 7.6% that day), about $2.26T market value. Google pays $920M a month for compute from October 2026. Very rich valuation; launch is the moat.

companies.name: Rocket Lab
companies.role: Electron and Neutron launch, satellite buses and components
companies.note: SDA awards above $1.3B; Neutron first launch no earlier than Q4 2026. Rich valuation.

companies.name: Firefly Aerospace
companies.role: Alpha small launcher, Blue Ghost lunar lander, Eclipse with Northrop
companies.note: Alpha returned to flight Mar 11, 2026 after the April 2025 failure. 2025 revenue $159.9M; 2026 guide $420M to $450M.

layers.name: Satellite communications and direct to cell
layers.why: Connectivity from space (broadband and phones) is the largest commercial space revenue pool, led by Starlink.
layers.bottleneck_reason: Spectrum is the scarce asset. SpaceX bought EchoStar's AWS-4, H-block and other spectrum for about $19.6B, and Amazon is buying Globalstar, so the land grab is mostly done.

companies.name: AST SpaceMobile
companies.role: Direct to smartphone broadband constellation (BlueBird)
companies.note: 13 BlueBirds launched through Aug 5, 2026; 14 to 16 shipping. Q2 2026 revenue $31.5M vs operating expenses $329.1M; 2026 guide $150M to $200M. Heavy capex and repeated convertible raises mean dilution.

companies.name: EchoStar
companies.role: Sold spectrum to SpaceX and AT&T; holds about 2% of SpaceX
companies.note: Up to about $11.1B of the SpaceX price was paid in SpaceX stock, so the market now trades SATS mostly as a SpaceX holding. Analyst values for the stake vary widely.

companies.name: Iridium Communications
companies.role: L band satellite voice and IoT
companies.note: Competitive threat from Starlink direct to cell, which had about 22M monthly mobile users by August 2026.

companies.name: Globalstar
companies.role: Apple emergency SOS satellite partner
companies.note: Apple put $1.1B into Globalstar plus a 20% stake for iPhone satellite features. Amazon agreed to buy Globalstar at $90 a share in cash (or 0.32 AMZN shares capped at $90), about $11.6B; expected to close in 2027.

companies.name: Viasat
companies.role: GEO and LEO broadband, defense communications
companies.note: Leverage; defense segment is the value driver.

layers.name: Defense space and Golden Dome
layers.why: Missile warning, tracking and space based interception are where the largest new government dollars are going.
layers.bottleneck_reason: Security clearances, classified programs and production scale limit the field to primes plus a few new entrants (SpaceX, Anduril, Palantir, Rocket Lab).

companies.name: Lockheed Martin
companies.role: Missile defense, SDA satellites, Next Gen OPIR
companies.note: About $1.1B SDA Tranche 3 tracking award; on the space based interceptor prototype list.

companies.name: Northrop Grumman
companies.role: SDA satellites, solid rocket motors, missile defense
companies.note: About $764M SDA Tranche 3 tracking award; on the space based interceptor prototype list; major solid rocket motor maker.

companies.name: L3Harris Technologies
companies.role: Missile tracking satellites, sensors, Aerojet Rocketdyne propulsion
companies.note: About $843M SDA Tranche 3 tracking award; owns Aerojet Rocketdyne propulsion.

companies.name: RTX
companies.role: Interceptors, radars, space sensors
companies.note: On the space based interceptor prototype list (as Raytheon).

companies.name: Palantir Technologies
companies.role: Software for defense command and control
companies.note: Software, not hardware; valuation is the main risk.

companies.name: Karman Holdings
companies.role: Missile and space subsystems supplier
companies.note: Smaller supplier; check valuation and float before acting.

layers.name: Space infrastructure, imaging and components
layers.why: Satellite buses, sensors, imaging data and in space infrastructure are the picks and shovels for both commercial and defense constellations.
layers.bottleneck_reason: Many suppliers, but space qualified components (solar arrays, star trackers, rad hard chips) have long qualification lead times.

companies.name: Planet Labs
companies.role: Daily Earth imaging constellation, defense customers

companies.name: BlackSky Technology
companies.role: High revisit imaging and analytics
companies.note: Small cap, dilution history.

companies.name: Redwire
companies.role: Space infrastructure, roll out solar arrays, drones
companies.note: Volatile small cap; check debt before acting.

companies.name: Intuitive Machines
companies.role: Lunar landers, NASA near space network
companies.note: Lumpy NASA dependent revenue.

companies.name: MDA Space
companies.role: Satellite buses, robotics (Canadarm)
companies.note: EchoStar cancelled its about $1.3B constellation contract in September 2025 after selling spectrum to SpaceX; MDA keeps the about $1.1B Globalstar constellation contract, which now sits under Amazon's pending purchase.

layers.name: Quantum computing hardware
layers.why: Governments and big tech are funding a race to fault tolerant machines; near term revenue is mostly government contracts and cloud access.
layers.bottleneck_reason: Talent, dilution refrigerators, lasers and isotopes are scarce, but no company controls a chokepoint and the winning modality (trapped ion, superconducting, neutral atom, photonic, annealing) is unknown.

companies.name: IBM
companies.role: Superconducting quantum roadmap, largest installed fleet
companies.note: Quantum is tiny vs IBM revenue; least speculative way to own quantum.

companies.name: Alphabet
companies.role: Google Quantum AI, Willow chip error correction

companies.name: Honeywell
companies.role: Majority owner of Quantinuum (trapped ion)
companies.note: Quantinuum listed June 4, 2026 (QNT) at $60, raising $1.68B; Honeywell and Cambridge Quantum Holdings kept about 82%.

companies.name: Quantinuum
companies.role: Trapped ion quantum computers (Helios) and software
companies.note: IPO June 4, 2026 at about $15.7B market value. 2025 revenue $30.9M, net loss $192.6M. Commerce Department CHIPS deal: $100M for a minority stake. Small float, mostly owned by Honeywell.

companies.name: IonQ
companies.role: Trapped ion systems; acquisitive (Oxford Ionics, SkyWater Technology)
companies.note: Q2 2026 revenue $80.1M, up 287%; 2026 standalone guide $280M to $290M (excludes SkyWater). Real growth, but still a high multiple and stock funded deals.

companies.name: Rigetti Computing
companies.role: Superconducting qubits
companies.note: Commerce Department CHIPS deal: $100M over three years for a minority stake. Revenue is still small.

companies.name: D-Wave Quantum
companies.role: Quantum annealing and gate model
companies.note: Commerce Department CHIPS deal: up to $100M for a minority stake, final agreement Sep 8, 2026.

companies.name: Quantum Computing Inc
companies.role: Photonic quantum and optics
companies.note: Minimal revenue; highest speculation risk.

layers.name: Cybersecurity platforms
layers.why: AI lets attackers automate phishing, reconnaissance and exploitation, and identity (human and machine) is the main attack path, so buyers consolidate onto platforms with endpoint, cloud, identity and SIEM in one.
layers.bottleneck_reason: Platform consolidation favors a few leaders, but the market stays competitive and big tech (Microsoft, Google with Wiz) bundles security.

companies.name: Palo Alto Networks
companies.role: Network, cloud, SOC and identity platform (CyberArk)
companies.note: Closed the about $25B CyberArk deal on Feb 11, 2026; market value passed about $330B in late September 2026.

companies.name: CrowdStrike
companies.role: Endpoint, cloud, identity and SIEM platform
companies.note: Premium valuation.

companies.name: Zscaler
companies.role: Zero trust secure access

companies.name: Fortinet
companies.role: Firewalls and secure networking with own ASICs
companies.note: Cheaper, hardware refresh cycle driven.

companies.name: Okta
companies.role: Workforce and customer identity

companies.name: Cloudflare
companies.role: Edge network, zero trust, AI bot defense
companies.note: Very high multiple.

companies.name: SentinelOne
companies.role: AI driven endpoint security
companies.note: Sub scale vs leaders.

companies.name: Microsoft
companies.role: Largest security vendor by revenue via bundles
companies.note: Bundles security into its cloud and Office suites.

companies.name: Check Point Software
companies.role: Firewalls and security management

second_order.idea: EchoStar trades as a SpaceX holding
second_order.why: EchoStar received up to about $11.1B of SpaceX stock for spectrum. SATS moves with SPCX, so it is a second way to own (or hedge) SpaceX, with legacy pay TV attached.

second_order.idea: SpaceX is also an AI compute landlord
second_order.why: Google pays SpaceX $920M a month for xAI data center compute from October 2026. Part of the SpaceX valuation now rides on AI capacity, not just rockets.

second_order.idea: Golden Dome favors propulsion and sensor chokepoints
second_order.why: Solid rocket motors and missile tracking satellites are capacity constrained, and these primes hold both the SDA tracking awards and interceptor prototype contracts.

second_order.idea: Post quantum cryptography is a near term cyber budget line
second_order.why: Federal migration to NIST post quantum standards creates spending now, long before quantum computers break encryption.
Gives exposure to the science without single stock dilution risk.

second_order.idea: Options angle: harvest premium in speculative space and quantum names
second_order.why: Implied volatility is very high. Covered calls on shares you already own or call spreads are safer than cash secured puts, because new share issuance can push prices down for months. Framework, not advice.

risks.risk: Dilution from at the market equity programs and convertibles
risks.signal: New ATM filings, share count growth each quarter, convertible issuance.

risks.risk: Valuation compression when rates rise or retail risk appetite fades
risks.signal: Price to sales vs peers; retail options volume; 10 year yield.
Neutron test milestones (first launch no earlier than Q4 2026), BlueBird launch dates, FAA mishap investigations.

risks.risk: Defense budget reprioritization, continuing resolutions or shutdowns
risks.signal: Appropriations progress; Golden Dome program milestones.

risks.risk: SpaceX vertical integration crowds out suppliers and competitors
risks.signal: Starlink Mobile monthly users (about 22M by August 2026, 25M target for year end) and carrier deals. Oct 8, 2026: SpaceX agreed to buy Grain Management's nationwide 800 MHz low band licenses (about $8B per WSJ, FCC approval pending); AT&T, Verizon and T-Mobile fell 5% to 7% after hours.

risks.risk: Quantum progress disappoints or big tech pulls ahead
risks.signal: Logical qubit and error rate milestones vs roadmaps (IBM Kookaburra in 2026); DARPA Quantum Benchmarking Initiative stage selections.

risks.risk: Cyber platform price wars and bundling by Microsoft and Google
risks.signal: Net revenue retention, billing growth deceleration.

risks.risk: Golden Dome cost gap: CBO's $1.2T estimate vs the administration's $185B
risks.signal: Appropriations language that caps or delays space based interceptor production.

Golden Dome and SDA contract awards
Defense appropriations status
indicators.why: Funding timing for all defense space names.

Quantum hardware milestones (logical qubits, error rates)
Cyber vendor ARR and net retention; major breach disclosures (SEC 8-K Item 1.05)
